# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ☝ 👏 🖐 👏 🖐 ✌ 👏 ✌ 👏 🖐 🖖 🙌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👏 🖐 🖖 👏 🖐 👏 ✌ 👏 🖐 ✌ 👏 🤟 👏 🙌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👏 🖐 ☝ 👏 🤟 👏 ✌ 👏 🖐 🖖 👏 🖐 ✌ 👏 🙌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 👏 🖖 👏 🖐 🖖 👏 ✌ 👏 🖐 ✌ 👏 🖐 👏 🙌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✌ 👏 🤟 👏 🖐 ☝ 👏 ✌ 👏 🖐 👏 🖐 ✌ 👏 🙌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🤟 👏 🖖 👏 🤟 👏 🖐 ✌ 👏 ✌ 👏 🖐 👏 🙌]

I can see the bomb’s current display, light, and the ordered wire colours. Mute’s gesture code is not yet decoded by me, so I should provide the visible facts aloud for both Mute and Blind to use with the manual and tactile controls.

``` 
speak(text="Visible bomb details: display reads 1. Light is green. Seven wires, in order: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute’s latest gesture is the standard five-finger sign, plausibly indicating wire 5 after receiving the display/light/wire details. I will relay that exact observable signal to Blind, while noting that it is Mute’s instruction rather than an action I can verify.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has just gestured the five-finger sign: 5. This appears to indicate wire 5; act only if that matches your manual-derived instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 5 was correctly cut, and the bomb has advanced to a new state. I should immediately give Mute and Blind the updated visible information so Mute can apply the manual to the next step.

``` 
speak(text="Update: wire 5 is cut correctly. New display reads 4; light is blue. Remaining wires: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute’s previous five-finger gesture correctly identified wire 5. The new gesture is 🤟, which is presumably Mute’s next coded wire instruction; given the remaining sequence, it likely denotes wire 6. I will relay it to Blind.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute now gestures 🤟. Their prior 🖐 instruction correctly meant cut wire 5. I infer this next symbol indicates wire 6; cut wire 6 if that is consistent with your controls/manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

The bomb has not changed since the correct cut of wire 5, so no further action has been confirmed. Mute first sent 🤟 and now sends three ☝ gestures. I cannot safely translate that gesture code into a wire number, so I will pass the exact latest signal to Blind rather than guess.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="No visible change: display 4, blue light, wire 5 cut. Mute's latest signal is three index-finger-up gestures: ☝ ☝ ☝. I cannot safely decode it; use it only if it matches your established instruction code.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

Mute appears to be clarifying the prior 🤟 instruction as “3”: it first used the three-finger gesture, then repeated three single-finger gestures and three thumbs-up gestures. The next intended wire is therefore wire 3, yellow.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is clarifying that the prior 🤟 means 3: they followed it with three ☝ and then three 👍. Cut wire 3, the yellow wire.")
```

System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 3 was correctly cut. The bomb has advanced again, so I will provide the updated visible state for Mute to determine the next instruction.

``` 
speak(text="Update: wire 3 yellow was cut correctly. New display reads 7; light is purple. Cut wires are 3 and 5. Remaining: 1 red, 2 white, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute’s single 👍 is consistent with the established counting clarification: one thumb-up means wire 1. The currently remaining wire 1 is red.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals 👍, which under their established counting clarification means 1. Cut wire 1, the red wire.")
```

LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

Wire 1 was correctly cut. The light changed from purple to green while the display remains 7. I will send the updated state to Mute and Blind.

``` 
speak(text="Update: wire 1 red was cut correctly. Display remains 7; light is now green. Cut wires: 1, 3, 5. Remaining wires: 2 white, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue.")
wait()
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

Mute is using repeated thumbs-up as a numeric instruction, as in the prior confirmed cuts. Seven thumbs-up indicates wire 7, which is blue.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals 👍 repeated seven times: 7. Cut wire 7, the blue wire.")
```
